title: The empty interface, `any` and the cost of losing the type

videos.script: Lesson 27 showed that a type satisfies an interface by having its methods. This lesson takes that rule to its limit. An interface with no methods at all is satisfied by every type, and Go calls it any. {{any}} You have used it already. fmt.Println takes it, and so does json.Unmarshal. Decode a JSON document into a map of any, and every number comes back as a float64, even an id that no longer fits in one. {{json}} Then the price. Once a value is inside an any, the compiler has forgotten its type. Adding two of them is refused. Getting the value back takes an assertion, and a wrong assertion compiles and panics when it runs. {{cost}} Last, the case that fools experienced programmers. An interface holding a nil pointer is not nil, and the check that should have caught it lets it through. {{nil}} By the end you will know when any is the right type, and why it rarely is.
